_note: Provider-price sensitivity scenarios. The workload is the shared pilot-traffic.json (10 entries); only the economic view changes. Each scenario is an isolated delta over pilot-catalog.json — nothing here mutates the base catalog or traffic. Scenario C (capacity-constrained) is deferred.

scenarios.label: Current pricing (Groq free tier)
scenarios.note: Groq llama-3.3-70b serves the cheap/generalist routes at $0. This is the real-world deployment the product currently assumes.

scenarios.label: Groq loses free tier (commercial price)
scenarios.note: The same routes now pay commercial Groq rates ($0.00059/$0.00079 per 1K, matching the system's fallback cost table).

scenarios.label: Groq unavailable
scenarios.note: Groq is removed entirely; the routes it served fall back to the next-cheapest paid model (gpt-4o-mini).

scenarios.label: Cache-aware economics (same route decisions, cache-capable models)
scenarios.note: Isolated cache-economics experiment: the SAME traffic and the SAME per-request route decisions as A, but the routes that contribute to B4 now resolve to paid, cache-capable models with explicit cacheHit rates (deepseek-v4-flash 0.1x cached-input, gpt-4o 0.1x cached-input on the adversarial floor). The adversarial-validation route is explicitly covered so EVERY route feeding B4 has a cacheHit — nothing leaks to an inherited catalog rate. cachedInputTokens in the traffic are measured (traffic default), so cache economics here do not depend on the 0.8 assumed ratio except for entries lacking measured cached counts. Holds 'same routing decisions + different cache economics'.
